 SCCH-26 3 MVC.2382/2023  JUDGMENT This claim petition is filed under the provisions of Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death of Smt. Lakshmi M., caused in a Road Traffic accident.
2.

The brief facts of the petitioners case are as under:
On 25.03.2023, at about 2.30 p.m., Smt.Lakshmi M., was standing at Madeshwara Stone Crusher, near Uttanahalli Betta, Uttanahalli Road, Jala Hobli, Bangalore, at that time the lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-02-D-3452 came in a rash and negligent manner in the revere direction and dashed against Smt. Lakshmi M.

Due to impact,
Lakshmi M., fell down, lorry was ran over her body and she died at the spot.
Deceased Lakshmi M., was aged about 36 years at the time of her death, she was working as a loader and unloader and earning Rs.18,000/- per month.
She has contributed her entire earnings to her family.
Due to sudden death of deceased, the petitioners have struggling for their livelihood.

The 2 nd respondent is the owner of lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-02-D-3252 and it was insured with the 1st respondent.
Hence, they have prayed to award compensation of Rs.45,00,000/- from the respondents.
4. The notice of the petition has been duly served on Respondents Nos.1 and 2.
Respondent Nos.1 and 2 have appeared before the court through their respective counsels.

Respondent No.1 has filed written statement, whereas respondent No.2 has not filed written statement and written statement of respondent No.2 is taken as nil.
5.
The Respondent No.1 has stated that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
This respondent has denied the lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-02-D- 3452 was involved in the alleged accident.
Further, denied the age, occupation and income of the deceased.
It is contended that, the accident was occurred solely due to rash and negligent driving of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA- 02-D-3452 by its driver.
The driver of lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-02-D-3452 was driving the same carefully, cautiously on the correct side of the road.
The accident took place within the premises of M/s Madeswara Stone Crusher, wherein the deceased was walking as a coolie at the time of accident.
The accident was not occurred in the public place, hence, the petition is not maintainable under the M.V. Act.
The 1st respondent has admitted the issuance of policy with respect to Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-02-D-3452 and it was valid from 19.10.2022 to 18.10.2023.
However, the liability of insurance company to indemnify the insured is with respect to terms, limitations and conditions of the policy.
It is stated that, there is no valid permit and FC to ply the Lorry bearing Rg.No.KA-02-D-3452 on the road as on the date of accident.
This respondent has called upon the 2nd respondent to prove the valid R.C., F.C., permit etc., with respect to Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-02-D-3452.
Further contended that,the owner of offending lorry willfully entrusted his vehicle to the person, who has not possessed valid and effective driving licence to drive the same on the date of accident.
The petition is bad for non-compliance of sec.158(6) and 134(c) of M.V. Act.
Further contended that, the deceased has contributed higher degree of negligence for the accident.
As such, the liability if any should considerably reduce by taking into consideration of higher degree of negligence on the part of deceased.

The compensation claimed by the petitioners is excessive,
imaginary and exorbitant.
Hence, he has prayed to dismiss the petition.

8. My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : In the Partly Affirmative Issue No.4 : As per final order for the following :

REASONS 9. ISSUE No.1:- PW.1 has produced Aadhaar Card of deceased at Ex.P.13 and it shows that, the petitioner No.1 is the husband of deceased Lakshmi M. P.W.1 has produced Aadhaar cards of petitioner No.2 to 4 at Ex.P.10 to Ex.P.12 respectively.
From these documents it is clear that,
petitioner Nos.2 to 4 are children of the deceased.
From these documents, it is clear that Petitioners No.1 to 4 are the legal heirs.
Therefore, petitioners No.1 to 4 are considered as dependents on the income of deceased.
Therefore, they are considered as legal heirs of deceased.
Hence, I answered the Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
10. ISSUE No.2:-

It is the case of PW.1 that, on 25.03.2023, at about 2.30 p.m., Smt. Lakshmi M.,
was standing at Madeshwara Stone Crusher, near Uttanahalli Betta, Uttanahalli Road, Jala Hobli,
Bangalore, at that time the lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-02-D-3452 came in a rash and negligent manner in the revere direction and dashed against Smt. Lakshmi M.
Due to impact, Lakshmi M., fell down, lorry was ran over her body and she died at the spot.
As already stated supra, the Petitioner No.1 has examined himself as PW.1.
He has filed affidavit in lieu of examination in chief and re-iterated the entire petition averments.

In support of his evidence, he has got marked 13 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13.
11.

After due investigation the police have filed charge-sheet against the driver of the above said Lorry for the offenses punishable U/s. 279 and 304-A of IPC as per Ex.P.8.
Ex.P.6 is the inquest panchanama.
Ex.P.7 is the postmortem report of the deceased and as per these documents, the cause of death is due to head injury due to road traffic accident.
Ex.P.5 is the Accident Inspection report which shows that, the cause of accident was not due to any mechanical defects.

15.
The petitioners have totally relied on the police documents to establish the negligence on the part of the offending vehicle's driver.
It is no doubt
the police have submitted the charge sheet against the driver of the offending lorry after thorough investigation.
The sketch appended to spot mahazar indicates that the driver of the offending vehicle was moving straight towards back side.
It is undisputed fact that the police have submitted that charge sheet against the driver of the offending lorry for the offense punishable U/sec. 279 and 304-A of IPC.
The oral evidence of the petitioners have coupled with documentary evidence.

16. At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

sentences.text: In view of the ratio laid down in the authorities refereed to above and applying the settled principle of law to the case at hand, which is further supported by the oral and documentary evidence adduced by PW-1, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident leading to this case indeed occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of lorry bearing Reg.No. KA-02-D-3452 resulting in death of the deceased.
During the course of cross examination of petitioner, except a suggestion nothing has been elicited so as to disprove the case of the petitioner.
There is no material evidence to prove that the deceased negligence was the reason for the said accident.

Even though the respondent examined its official as RW1, the evidence of RW1 is based on the police documents and RW1 is not an eyewitness, hence, the evidence of RW1 failed to rebut the case of the petitioners in respect of the fact of accident and the negligence of the driver of offending Lorry bearing Reg.No. KA-02-D-3452.
18.
As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, deceased Lakshmi was died in the accident took place on 25-03-2023 which is caused by the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg. No. KA-02-D-3452.
There are no reasons to discard the evidence of petitioners.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
19. Therefore, there is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is collusive or defective and the evidence of PW-1 corroborates with the documents produced by him.
There is nothing elicited to disprove the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compared to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the chapter in M.V.Act dealing with compensation is a benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
Therefore, based on the above discussion, I hold that the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No. KA-02-D-3452 is proved.
As such, I answer issue No.2 in the Affirmative.
20. ISSUE No.3:

As already discussed in Issue No.1, Petitioner No.1 to 4 are the dependents of the deceased Lakshmi M., and they are entitled for compensation.
21. LOSS OF DEPENDENCY:- PW.1 has produced the notarized copy of Aadhaar card of deceased at Ex.P.13.
As per this document, the deceased was born in the year 1986.
The accident was occurred on 25.03.2023.
Therefore, as on the date of accident deceased Lakshmi M., was 37 years.

As per the principles laid down by their Lordships in 2009 ACJ 1298 (Sarla Verma Vs Delhi Transport Corporation), the multiplier applicable to the present case is '15'.
22.

sentences.text: REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.
28. Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2 is the owner and respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Lorry bearing Reg No.KA-02-D-3452 the accident has occurred and the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.

29 . But, the respondent No.1 insurance company has taken specific contentions in its written statement that, as on the date of accident the driver of the offending lorry was not having valid permit to ply the same at the place of accident.
As there is breach of conditions of the policy, the respondent No.1-insurance company is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.2.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the respondent No.2 to prove that, at the time of accident, his vehicle was having valid permit to ply the same at the place of accident.
But, the respondent No.2 has failed to discharge his burden in the case.

The respondent No.2 has neither stepped into witness box to adduce his evidence, nor he has produced any document to show that, at the time of accident his vehicle was having valid permit to ply the same at the place of accident.

On the other hand, in order to establish the said contentions, the respondent No.1 has examined the official of RTO office,
Yalahanka as R.W.2.

R.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the permit issued by his office with respect of Lorry bearing Reg No.KA-02-D-3452 was valid from 11-07- 2017 to 10-07-2022 and as on 25-03-2023, the said permit was not in force.
He has also produced true copy of permit with fee details of Lorry bearing Reg No.KA-02-D-3452 which is marked as Ex.R.4.

As per Ex.R.4 Permit,
as on the date of accident the offending Lorry bearing Reg No.KA-02- D-3452 was not having valid permit to ply the said vehicle at the place of accident.
30. The respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle is appeared, but not filed any written statement and contested the matter.
The respondent No.2 has not made out any grounds to show that there was a valid permit at the time of accident.

The oral answers of petitioners is not sufficient to consider that there was a valid permit for the offending vehicle at the time of accident because, the documents produced at Ex.R-4,being the public documents clearly establishes that as on the date of accident, there was no valid permit for the offending Lorry bearing Reg No.KA-02-D-3452.
31.

The respondent No.1 insurance company has taken specific defence of non existence of permit to the offending vehicle and also taken steps to prove that, the offending vehicle has no permit at the time of accident.
The respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence by showing the existence of permit to the offending vehicle.
Hence, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability.

sentences.text: By keeping the arguments canvassed by both the parties in background, there is no dispute that at the time of accident the Lorry bearing Reg No.KA-02-D-3452 was covered with insurance.
But the violation of the condition of insurance policy is stands established.

33. This Court also finds that since the contract of insurance is between insurer and the owner and has no concern with the claimants who are in fact victims of the accident, language used in section 149 (prior to amendment) and section 150 (after amendment) would show that notwithstanding the fact that the insurer may be entitled to avoid or cancel the policy on account of breach of terms thereof, it shall pay to the person entitled to the benefit of the award.
Therefore, whether Insurance Company cancels or does not cancel an insurance policy, the same has nothing to do with the claimants and they are entitled to get the amount from insurer.

It means that claimants' right to receive compensation from the insurer at the first instance is unaffected by the inter-se rights and liabilities arising out of contract between the insurer and the owner.
34. Further in the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in 2022 ACJ 2771 between Gohar Mohammed V/s U.P State Road Transportation Corporation & others wherein it is held as follows:

entities.text: Gohar Mohammed V/s U.P State Road Transportation Corporation & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "8. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the material available on record, it clearly reveals that on the date of accident, the appellant did not have a valid and effective permit to ply the offending vehicle on the route where accident took place.

Having extensively gone through the factfinding exercise, it is categorically recorded by MACT that the appellant was neither able to produce/prove the original permit nor was able to prove the information received under RTI Act.
Even if RTI information is considered by which it is not clear as to when the disputed permit was issued and by whom.

The alleged permit was issued on 28.07.2012, i.e.,
on Saturday and no explanation is on record as to why deposit of fee was asked on the next day i.e. Sunday.

Moreover, assuming that permit was valid as per letter of Transport Authority, but it does not of any help to the appellant since the vehicle was being plied on a route different than specified in permit.

The appellant has failed to give any explanation to refute the observations made by MACT to ply the vehicle on Roorkee bypass to Haridwar via Meerut which did not fall within the route of permit issued by Transport Authority.
The said findings of fact have been affirmed by the High Court by the impugned order.

9. After going through the record, the concurrent findings of fact do not warrant any interference since they do not outrageously defy the logic as to suffer from the vice of irrationality and neither incur the blame of being perverse.
In view of foregoing discussion, we are of the considered opinion that the arguments raised by appellant are bereft of any merit, hence this appeal is hereby dismissed".

35. In this case, the respondent No.2 owner of the Lorry bearing Reg No.KA-02-D-3452 even after the service of summons has not lead any evidence to show that he has not violated the policy condition willfully.

Thereby the conduct of respondent No.2 -owner allowing the Lorry bearing Reg No.KA-02-D-3452 to ply on the road without permit is a breach of policy condition and thereby the Shiva Kumar B.D vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55497642/
9 insurance company cannot be fastened with liability.

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 being the owner cannot take the benefit of his own wrong.

Under such circumstances, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability of pay and recover when there is clear breach of rules of IMV Act and liability to pay compensation is on the respondent No.2 owner.
Hence, the respondent No.2 owner is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The petitioners are entitle for compensation of Rs.32,52,000/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, I answer issue No.3 partly in the Affirmative.
36. ISSUE No.4:- In view of my findings on issue No.1 to 3, I proceed pass the following:
: : ORDER ::
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners ares entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.32,52,000/-
(Rupees thirty two lakh fifty two thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of deposit the award amount.
The respondent No.2 owner is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
The petition against respondent No.1-insurance company stands dismissed.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 55% Petitioner No.2 - 15% Petitioner No.3 - 15% Petitioner No.4 - 15 %

Out of the total compensation amount, 25% of the apportionment amount shall be kept in FD in the name of petitioner No.1 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years and balance 75% shall be disbursed to him through E- payment on proper identification.
However the said Petitioner No.1 is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.

Since the petitioner No.2 to 4 are minors, the entire share amount of Petitioner No.2 to 4 shall be deposited in their names as FD in any nationalized /scheduled bank till they are attaining the age of majority.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.

There is no material evidence to prove that the deceased negligence was the reason for the said accident.
Even though the respondent examined its official as RW1, the evidence of RW1 is based on the police documents and RW1 is not an eyewitness, hence, the evidence of RW1 failed to rebut the case of the petitioners in respect of the fact of accident and the negligence of the driver of offending Lorry bearing Reg.No. KA-02-D-3452.
18.
As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.
All the materials available on record leading to show that, deceased Lakshmi was died in the accident took place on 25-03-2023 which is caused by the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg. No. KA-02-D-3452.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
There is nothing elicited to disprove the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compared to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision of Yashoda.H and others V/s. Sharath Kumar Achar and another.
Therefore in view of the above decision the notional income of Shiva Kumar B.D vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55497642/
6
Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Lorry bearing Reg No.KA-02-D-3452 the accident has occurred and the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
As there is breach of conditions of the policy, the respondent No.1-insurance company is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.2.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the respondent No.2 to prove that, at the time of accident, his vehicle was having valid permit to ply the same at the place of accident.
But, the respondent No.2 has failed to discharge his burden in the case.
The respondent No.2 has neither stepped into witness box to adduce his evidence, nor he has produced any document to show that, at the time of accident his vehicle was having valid permit to ply the same at the place of accident.
The respondent No.2 has not made out any grounds to show that there was a valid permit at the time of accident.
The oral answers of petitioners is not sufficient to consider that there was a valid permit for the offending vehicle at the time of accident because, the documents produced at Ex.R-4,being the public documents clearly establishes that as on the date of accident, there was no valid permit for the offending Lorry bearing Reg No.KA-02-D-3452.
31.
The respondent No.1 insurance company has taken specific defence of non existence of permit to the offending vehicle and also taken steps to prove that, the offending vehicle has no permit at the time of accident.
The respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence by showing the existence of permit to the offending vehicle.
Hence, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability.

9 insurance company cannot be fastened with liability.
Under such circumstances, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability of pay and recover when there is clear breach of rules of IMV Act and liability to pay compensation is on the respondent No.2 owner.
